name: v2ecoli-vecoli-comparison
title: v2ecoli ↔ vEcoli comparison
question: Does v2ecoli reproduce vEcoli across nutrient conditions?

executive.what_is_this:
Does v2ecoli reproduce vEcoli across nutrient conditions? Each study runs both engines from matched ParCa initial states and grades v2ecoli against a live vEcoli reference on cell, dry, protein and RNA mass, and growth rate. GOLD STANDARD: grading gates on the multi-seed STATISTICAL card (Welch t-test over 4 seeds) plus the ParCa t=0 card; the single-seed card is illustrative only.

HEADLINE (resolved): v2ecoli now reproduces vEcoli across all five conditions. The multi-seed grading first revealed a real, bidirectional off-basal divergence -- v2 over-grew on poor carbon (acetate growth +40%, p=0.049) and under-grew on rich amino acids (with_aa growth -16% / RNA -21%, p<0.01), matching only at the basal ParCa fit point. We traced it end to end and FIXED it at the source; after the fix every condition reproduces vEcoli with no statistically significant divergence remaining.

RESULT (4-seed gen-1, before -> after fix):
  basal      within_tol -> within_tol   (control; fix preserves the fit point)
  acetate    MISMATCH (growth +40.2%, p=0.049) -> drift (+15.9%, p=0.28, not significant); RNA/cell/dry/protein within_tol
  with_aa    MISMATCH (growth -16.1% p=0.003, RNA -21.3% p=0.001) -> within_tol on ALL five observables
  succinate  drift (growth +18.0%, p=0.06) -> drift (-6.6%, p=0.44, not significant); 4/5 within_tol
  no_oxygen  drift (growth +14.4%, p=0.08) -> drift (+6.7%, p=0.50, not significant); 4/5 within_tol
Both significant mismatches are eliminated; the borderline drifts are halved to basal-level, non-significant residuals.

ROOT CAUSE (pinned): the RNAP core complex (APORNAP-CPLX) is limited by its rpoB/rpoC subunits. v2's ParCa fit set exp_free[rpoBC operon]=0 -- a non-negativity BOUNDARY solution of the cistron->TU NNLS in Transcription.set_ppgpp_expression (a fit step the code itself flags as non-reproducible across numpy/scipy builds). That zeroed free-expression term is inconsistent with rpoBC's own ppGpp fold-change (-1.08/-0.76: ppGpp represses rpoBC, so exp_free must exceed exp_ppgpp). Because expression_from_ppgpp = f(ppGpp)*exp_ppgpp + (1-f)*exp_free, the split is pinned equal at the basal setpoint but inverts rpoBC's nutrient response off-basal -- compressing assembled APORNAP-CPLX -> active_RNAP -> rRNA/growth. Verified: the ppGpp coupling code, ppGpp setpoint, doubling times, active-RNAP fraction and aa-supply are all identical between engines; the divergence was this single degenerate fit term. (rpoA/sigma/rpoZ and ribosomal genes fit correctly, which is why PROTEIN MASS reproduces throughout -- the tell that isolated the defect to rRNA/ribosome allocation, not translation.)

THE FIX: scripts/fix_ppgpp_rpobc_expression.py re-partitions the rpoBC operon's expression into a fold-change-consistent, basal-preserving split (ratio exp_ppgpp/exp_free ~0.40) -- self-contained (no reference cache), idempotent. It restores rpoBC per-condition expression from {basal 1.0, with_aa 0.37, acetate 1.44} back to ~1.0 vs vEcoli, and assembled APORNAP-CPLX from {acetate 1.45, with_aa 0.37} to {0.99, 1.02} with basal unchanged. All 'after fix' runs above are v2ecoli NATIVE on its own corrected fit -- no vEcoli seeding. Durable follow-up: harden the NNLS boundary in set_ppgpp_expression so a full ParCa regeneration cannot reintroduce it. (Also open: a pre-existing anaerobic-FBA numerical edge -- BIOTIN homeostatic target ~ -2e-6 -- tripped 2 no_oxygen seeds; unrelated to the fix, graded on the clean seeds.)

The MetabolismRedux swap remains investigated-but-blocked on a process-bigraph step-cascade runtime issue (not a science mismatch).

studies.name: metabolism_redux
studies.title: v2ecoli reproduces vEcoli with MetabolismRedux (basal, short-horizon)
studies.question: Does v2ecoli reproduce vEcoli on basal when both engines swap FBA Metabolism for MetabolismRedux?

findings.statement: BLOCKED on a runtime issue, not wiring. Both engines correctly swap FBA Metabolism -> MetabolismRedux (vEcoli native via EcoliSim; v2ecoli via convert+inject bridge). The v2-side run is fast on tick 1 (~1.3 s) but degrades to 25-45 s/tick from tick 2 on, making even a 300-step run impractical (~a day for a full 2-gen run).

evidence.observed: CORRECTED root cause (supersedes the earlier ODE-fallback theory): it is a process-bigraph STEP-CASCADE NON-CONVERGENCE, not an ODE/units/allocator problem. Measured: ~170,000+ Composite.apply_updates rounds per tick under redux. A FIXED GROUP of ~8 steps re-runs together in equal counts (~3,750x/tick, climbing): ecoli-equilibrium, ecoli-two-component-system, ecoli-rna-maturation, unique_update_1..4, media_update. The re-trigger driver is the unique-molecule /update stores (unique/active_RNAP/update, .../RNA/update, .../active_ribosome/update, chromosome/replisome/oriC/promoter) flipping every round. Each round is fast (~0 s); the COUNT is the 25-45 s. Baseline (no redux): equilibrium runs ~1x/tick, the cascade converges, done. Redux tick-2+: the run_steps recursion (run_steps -> apply_updates -> cycle_step_state re-arms triggered steps -> run_steps) never reaches a fixed point. EVERYTHING EARLIER WAS A DOWNSTREAM SYMPTOM of those ~170k tiny rounds — the "LSODA stiffness" was 170k tiny solves, the "cProfile plum/schema" was 170k tiny dispatches. RULED OUT (all, with evidence): ODE stiffness; JIT (cost is step-count not RHS speed); horizon cap (breaks equilibrium: "Negative values at equilibrium steady state"); bridge units (CORRECT — cell_mass=1269 fg, boundary.external[GLC]=11.1 mM, counts_to_molar sane); output_ports; negative bulk counts (clamp fired 0x); the two-component no-allocator fallback; PARTITIONING (would not fix a cascade loop — a partition design was drafted then abandoned); the redux flow reorder (removing it did NOT help); zeroing Equilibrium.update bulk output (did NOT break the loop — eq still participates via being triggered). => the metabolism_redux PROCESS SWAP itself perturbs the step trigger/deriver network so the reconciliation cascade does not terminate. NOT YET PINNED: the exact closing trigger edge (which step's write re-arms which via the unique /update stores). Fix paths: (true) trace the closing edge — a unique_update deriver / listener that redux's presence keeps re-arming; (pragmatic unblock) a max-iteration cap in process_bigraph.composite.run_steps to bound the cascade (risks slightly-incomplete reconciliation). Full evidence chain in project memory project_metabolism_redux_injection_ode_stiffness.

derived.insight: BLOCKED on a runtime issue, not wiring. Both engines correctly swap FBA Metabolism -> MetabolismRedux (vEcoli native via EcoliSim; v2ecoli via convert+inject bridge). The v2-side run is fast on tick 1 (~1.3 s) but degrades to 25-45 s/tick from tick 2 on, making even a 300-step run impractical (~a day for a full 2-gen run).
